smoking_behavior.quit_intention: Will quit in the next month

rated_messages.input_message: Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
Notice what it feels like to see other people smoke and choose not to smoke. Notice what thoughts or emotions come up. Allow them to come and go. They will pass and so will this urge.
You don’t need to get rid of or change your thoughts about smoking—just let them pass by like a cloud in the sky.
You were often stressed in this location and this might trigger urges. What can you do to reduce your stress here? If you can avoid this place until things settle down, then do.
Pause and take 5 slow breaths. Pausing just for a moment breaks the automatic habit of reaching for a smoke.
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.

To keep on track, small changes can really help. For example, keep a list of quit reasons where you used to keep cigarettes, rearrange your living space, or grab some extra pens to fiddle with to keep your hands busy.
If you get urges, remind yourself that cigarettes did that to you. If you go back to them, they will keep making you suffer. Now you are breaking free.
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, try taking the next call in a place where you can't smoke and focus on the conversation. The urge will pass.
